results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Bringer of the Last Gift, Superior Spider-Man and Town Greeter.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and how real decks have played them.

The three cards don't appear together in any published list. Town Greeter's main home is Golgari Roots, and Spider-Man is blue-black, so I'll check those shells and the field.

Golgari Roots is the closest shell for Town Greeter and Bringer. Spider-Man is blue-black, so I'll also check the Rogue list (it has one Spider-Man list) and the mill and reanimation enablers.

Here's where the three directions stand:

- **Golgari mill-reanimate** (Town Greeter, Overlord of the Balemurk, Dredger's Insight, Molt Tender, Insidious Roots): the strongest fit, since Town Greeter is green and Bringer and Spider-Man both want creatures in the graveyard.
- **Dimir Spider-Man midrange** (Floodpits Drowner, Spyglass Siren, Kaito): fits Spider-Man's colors, but it has almost no mill and cannot play Town Greeter.
- **Rogue**: has one Spider-Man list and no graveyard plan, so it's a weak base.

I'll build the Golgari direction. Next I'll look for more black-green creatures, graveyard recursion and removal that are legal in Standard.

Honest Rutstein, Osteomancer Adept, Assassin's Trophy, Feed the Swarm and Bitter Triumph all look usable. Next I'll confirm the mana base and check Bringer's odds.

Two findings change the build. Llanowar Wastes is not legal in Standard, and Superior Spider-Man costs {2}{U}{B}, so the deck needs a blue splash. I'll check the legal blue lands before choosing the mana.

Watery Grave, Undercity Sewers, Gloomlake Verge, Restless Reef and Island are all legal blue sources, so the splash is covered. Next I'll check the sideboard candidates before running the deck check.

Go for the Throat is not legal, so I'll leave it out. Next I'll run the deck check on the full 60 with a 15-card sideboard, comparing its mana to Golgari Roots.

The check passes with no errors or warnings. Two things stand out: green has 16 sources against Golgari Roots' 21, and the tool suggests about 23.5 lands. I'll swap Cache Grab for a Forest to reach 23 lands and add green consistency.

Both checks are clean with 23 lands and no warnings. I'll submit the deck.

The checker flagged three cards as rarely played, so I'll resubmit with a reason for keeping each one.

I submitted a Golgari mill-and-reanimate brew with a blue splash for Superior Spider-Man. It is a brew, not a proven list: no published deck runs these three cards together, and Golgari Roots is only 0.3% of the current field.

**The plan:** Town Greeter and Overlord of the Balemurk fill the graveyard with creatures and return Bringer to hand. Llanowar Elves, Molt Tender and Honest Rutstein get Bringer to 7–8 mana, and its cast trigger returns every creature card from both graveyards. Superior Spider-Man copies the best creature in a graveyard for 4 mana.

**Direction:** I weighed three options. Golgari reanimation fit Town Greeter and Bringer best, Dimir Spider-Man had almost no mill, and Rogue had no graveyard plan. I borrowed Golgari Roots' mill and ramp package and added the blue splash that Spider-Man needs.

**Honest odds:** The win line is slow. The tool's estimate is that all six line cards are drawn by turn 8 in only 1.5% of games, so this is a long-game deck that needs several draws to come together. Three removal and cost-reduction cards were flagged as rarely played; I kept them because each does a job the others do not.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Mightform Harmonizer, Spell Snare and Full Bore.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and what real decks run them with.

The three cards don't appear together in any published list. I'll check the landfall and warp support, and the Landfall and Boros Aggro shells.

Three directions fit the request:

- **A. Temur landfall-warp:** green carries Harmonizer and the Landfall package, red brings Full Bore and burn, and blue is a light Spell Snare splash.
- **B. Izzet tempo (U/R):** Spell Snare and Full Bore fit, but Harmonizer doesn't.
- **C. Boros aggro:** Full Bore fits, but Harmonizer and Spell Snare don't.

Direction A is the only one that uses all three cards centrally. I'll check the cards it needs.

The Landfall shell gives me a green base with fetchlands and Llanowar Elves. I'll draft the list and run the checker against it.

The checker passes with no errors or warnings. Blue sources are 9 counting fetches, and the draw odds are honest: Harmonizer by turn 4 is about 53%. Submitting.

The checker wants a reason for not building the Boros shell that most Full Bore lists use. I'll add one and resubmit.

I submitted a Temur brew: green landfall creatures with red burn and a light blue splash, built on the Landfall shell. The deck is 24 lands and 36 spells, and it passed the checker with no errors or warnings.

I chose this direction because it is the only one of three that uses all three cards centrally. The alternatives were an Izzet tempo build, which drops Harmonizer, and a Boros build, which drops Harmonizer and Spell Snare.

The plan is to ramp with Llanowar Elves and warp Mightform Harmonizer on turn 3 or 4. A land drop doubles its power, and Full Bore then gives it trample and haste because it was warped. Nova Hellkite, Burst Lightning and Lightning Strike handle the rest.

The odds are modest. Harmonizer is in hand or drawn by turn 4 about 53% of the time, and Harmonizer plus Full Bore together about 27%. The full four-turn win line is drawn only about 1% of the time, so this is a midrange-leaning deck that wins on card quality, not a reliable turn-4 kill. Spell Snare is only a narrow counter, and two copies with nine blue sources is the most I could justify.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Insatiable Avarice, Doomsday Excruciator and Archenemy's Charm.
results.text:
Submitted a mono-black control brew built around the three cards, borrowing the black removal and creatures from Dimir Midrange and dropping its blue.

**Plan:** Survive on cheap black removal (Heartless Act, Murder, Hero's Downfall, Bitter Triumph, Shoot the Sheriff, Archenemy's Charm) and flyers (Vampire Nighthawk, Qarsi Revenant, Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Aclazotz). Then land Doomsday Excruciator, which leaves both libraries at six cards, and finish with a 6-power flyer, using Archenemy's Charm to clear a flying blocker. Insatiable Avarice's BB mode (opponent draws three and loses three) adds reach and speeds their deck-out.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three. Tuned Dimir Midrange puts blue in the deck, which strains the BBBBBB cost of Excruciator. B/G Reanimator doesn't use Excruciator well, since reanimating it skips the mill. Mono-black gives the most reliable mana for the requested cards and still has enough playable black creatures and removal.

**Caveats:**
- Excruciator's mill is symmetric. You draw two cards a turn (upkeep plus draw step) against their one, so you can deck about as fast as they do. Plan to end the game within about three turns of landing it.
- I ran only two copies because BBBBBB with 23 Swamps is hard to cast on time. My rough estimate is about half the time you have six black sources by turn 8; the tools don't give exact counts for that, so treat it as an estimate.
- The line (six Swamps, then Excruciator, Charm on a blocker, attack for 6, Avarice) is drawn in only about 15% of games by turn 8, so expect it to be a late-game plan.

I built a Rakdos (black-red) aggro deck around Iron-Shield Elf, Bloodthorn Flail and Flamewake Phoenix, and the submission was accepted as a brew.

No real list runs these three cards together; Flail and Phoenix each appear only in a few Rogue lists.

That power-4 creature turns on Flamewake Phoenix's Ferocious, so the Phoenix can keep returning from the graveyard for R. Burst Lightning, Lightning Strike, Abrade and Bitter Triumph clear blockers, and Terror of the Peaks and Bonehoard Dracosaur close the game. No published Standard list runs these three together, so this is a brew: the Dwarf and Equipment package is my own, and only the mana (Sacred Foundry, Sundown Pass) and the Boros Weapons mana base are borrowed from the field.

**Direction chosen:** Red-white Dwarves, over a mono-red Dwarf list (which would drop Kíli, Dáin's Company and Giott) and over a straight Boros Weapons clone (which would lose the Dwarf engine). Every creature is a Dwarf, so Kíli draws off almost any creature or Equipment entering, and Dáin's Company tutors from roughly 32 Dwarf or Equipment targets.

**Plan:** Mauler on turn 1, Kíli on turn 2, then Dwarven Mattock on turn 3 attaching to a Dwarf for +2/+2 and ward while Kíli draws. Fíli's anthem and the Thorin, Mountain-king equip-and-burn take over from turn 4. Cheap removal (Erode, Lightning Strike, Chainsaw, Mjölnir) clears blockers.

**Odds:** On the play, a Mattock or Dáin's Company is in hand by turn 3 about 75% of the time, and Kíli about 49%. The winning sequence (Mauler, Kíli, Mattock, Fíli, Thorin) is completed by turn 5 in about 0.5% of games, so this is a shell that needs its engine cards to show up; the odds are low and I'd expect it to play out more as a grindy midrange deck.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Greedy Freebooter, The Sackville-Bagginses and Umbral Collar Zealot.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and how they've been played.

The three cards form a sacrifice package: Freebooter is a 1-drop that makes a Treasure when it dies, Sackville draws off a sacrifice, and Zealot turns every extra creature or artifact into surveil. Next I'll check the field and the sac-related cards that are legal.

The field has a lot of sac-adjacent black cards. I'll check the ones from the little-played list plus a few sac payoffs and fodder makers.

Bloodghast is the strongest sac-engine piece (Mardu Discard runs it in 102 lists), and Treasures from Freebooter count as tokens for Sackville's drain. Next I'll look at the black-based shells and at black removal.

I have the three directions mapped. Before choosing, I'll confirm the removal and top-end cards I'm considering, and pull the exact text on the remaining candidates.

The removal in the field is mostly black (Bitter Triumph is in 10.5% of recent lists, Shoot the Sheriff in 8.9%), so I'll take Bitter Triumph and Hero's Downfall. Now I'll check the 60-card draft.

The check passed with no errors. It recommends 23.2 lands; I'm running 22, because four Freebooters and Sackville's Treasure already add mana and the curve tops out at 6. Next I'll check the sideboard and run an odds check on the early sac engine.

The sideboard is one card over. I'll cut Eaten Alive, then check how often the early engine shows up.

Both checks pass. Submitting the brew with the sideboard now.

I built a mono-black sacrifice deck around the three requested cards (a brew, since no published list runs them together). It's 22 lands and 38 spells, with a 15-card sideboard.

**The plan:** Freebooter, Sackville-Bagginses and Zealot turn every spare creature, Treasure or token into card selection and drain. Bloodghast returns on each land drop and feeds the Zealot, and Infestation Sage and Bitterbloom Bearer add more fodder. Heartless Act, Bitter Triumph and Hero's Downfall handle threats, while Vein Ripper and Massacre Wurm drain the opponent each time a creature dies. The win line runs to turn 6.

**Direction chosen:** Mono-black over Mardu Discard (it shares Bloodghast but needs white and red) and over a Dimir blue-splash build. All three requested cards are black, so a single colour keeps the sacrifice engine reliable. Bitter Triumph (in 10.5% of recent lists) and Shoot the Sheriff (8.9%) confirm black removal is well played in the field.

**Caveats:**
- Only about 44% of games show a Freebooter by turn 2 on the play.
- I ran 22 lands against the checker's 23.2 recommendation, because four Freebooters and Sackville's Treasure add mana.
- This is untested against the field, so treat the win line as a plan, not a proven result.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Sentinel of the Nameless City, Abrupt Decay and Tear Asunder.
results.text:
I submitted a Golgari midrange brew (23 lands, 3 Llanowar Elves) built around Sentinel of the Nameless City, Abrupt Decay and Tear Asunder. The plan is to land Sentinel on turn 3 or Sheoldred on turn 4, use Fatal Push, Abrupt Decay and Assassin's Trophy to clear blockers and threats, then win with Sheoldred's drain and Vraska, Golgari Queen in the late game.

I chose this direction over two alternatives: a Golgari sacrifice build borrowing Jund Sacrifice's Witch's Oven and Scavenger's Talent package, and a Selesnya ramp deck splashing black for the kicker. Those would bury Sentinel or leave the black mana too thin. No published list runs all three requested cards, so this is a brew. It borrows Jund Sacrifice's mana and removal, plus the green elves and Badgermole Cub from Selesnya Company.

Things you should know:
- **Cori-Steel Cutter is banned in Pioneer** according to the card database, even though the Izzet Prowess list in your menu includes it. That list is stale or wrong, so Prowess may be weaker than the 35% share suggests.
- **Assassin's Trophy** drew a note because Go for the Throat is the usual pick. I kept two copies on purpose: Trophy is the only instant here that hits planeswalkers like Teferi and The Wandering Emperor, which UW Control runs.
- **Odds are modest.** On the play, you have Sentinel by turn 4 about 53% of the time and Sheoldred about 43%. The full win line is drawn by turn 6 in only about 1.5% of games, so this is a midrange deck that needs a few turns to assemble.
- The sideboard has 15 cards aimed at Prowess and control, including Putrefy and Thrashing Brontodon for artifacts and enchantments.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Igneous Inspiration, Combustion Technique and Abandon Attachments.
results.text:
I built an Izzet Lessons-Prowess deck that uses the Izzet Prowess core (Swiftspear, Soul-Scar Mage, Emberheart Challenger, Screaming Nemesis, Stormchaser's Talent) around the three requested cards. Labelled brew, with Izzet Prowess as the donor shell.

**Direction chosen:** Izzet Prowess. Three directions were possible: Izzet Prowess with Lessons, mono-red Lessons, or a Rogue-style deck. I picked Izzet Prowess because Abandon Attachments already sits in about 79 of its lists, and it is the densest shell for cheap noncreature spells that trigger prowess.

**The plan:** Cheap creatures attack and get prowess pumps from the cheap spells. Abandon Attachments loots away extra lands and goes to the graveyard as a Lesson. That fuels Combustion Technique (2 damage plus one for each Lesson in your graveyard, exiling the creature), which clears blockers. Igneous Inspiration's 3 damage to any target finishes the game.

**Things to know:**
- Cori-Steel Cutter, the most-played card in Izzet Prowess, shows as **banned** in this Pioneer data, so I left it out.
- The main deck runs 21 lands (16 blue sources, 21 red) and passed `check_deck` with no errors or warnings.
- The win line is on turn 5 and is a plan, not a tested result. The tool reports that all cards in the line have been drawn by turn 5 in only 0.8% of games.

results.prompt: Brew me a Modern deck built around Thud, Plunge into Darkness and Spoils of the Vault.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and how they've been played.

The three cards are a sacrifice package: Thud needs a creature to sacrifice, Plunge can sacrifice creatures for life, and Spoils is a one-card tutor. I'll look at what fits around them, starting with reanimation, big creatures, and sacrifice outlets.

Spoils of the Vault tutors one named card, so the cleanest shell is a reanimation plan that puts a big creature into the graveyard, then uses Thud to sacrifice it for damage. Next I'll check which reanimation spells, discard, and fatties are legal in Modern.

Entomb, Animate Dead, Reanimate, and Cabal Therapy are not legal in Modern, so the classic black reanimator is out. Grixis Persist is the closest live shell: it already has black, red for Thud, and reanimation. I'll pull its list and the other candidates.

Grixis Persist (5-0 in a Modern League, and 126 lists in the last 30 days) is my donor shell. I'll confirm the reanimation and fodder cards it uses before I build around them.

The line I'm building around is Persist returning Archon of Cruelty, which triggers on entering and attacking, then Thud sacrificing it for damage. I'll check the sideboard cards I want and the lands, then run the list through the checker.

All the sideboard cards and lands are legal. Next I'll run the full 60 and the 15-card sideboard through the checker, comparing its mana to Grixis Persist.

The checker flags a light land count for an 8-mana finisher, so I'll go to 20 lands by trimming one Spell Pierce and adding a Swamp, then re-check.

The checker is clean at 20 lands. I'll check the odds for the core pieces: Archon of Cruelty and Persist by turn 6.

The line works but is inconsistent: a turn-6 Archon-and-Persist hand is about 60%, and all three pieces together are about 12%. I'll state that plainly. Submitting now.

I built a Grixis brew on the Grixis Persist shell (the reanimation deck that has been 5-0 in a recent Modern League), with Thud, Plunge into Darkness and Spoils of the Vault added as sacrifice-and-recursion finishers. The win line is Faithless Looting discarding Archon of Cruelty, Persist returning it, attacking to repeat its triggers, then Thud sacrificing it for 5 to the face on turn 6. This is a brew with no proven list behind the three requested cards, and it is inconsistent: Archon and Persist are both in hand by turn 6 about 60% of the time, and all of Archon, Persist and Thud together only about 12%.

Notes on the three requested cards:
- **Spoils of the Vault** costs one life for every card it exiles before the named card. Naming a card with four copies costs roughly 11 life on average, so I played only two copies and named Archon.
- **Thud** is a one-shot finisher that needs a big creature to sacrifice, so it runs only two copies.
- **Plunge into Darkness** gives 3 life per creature it sacrifices and doubles as card advantage, which helps offset Spoils' life cost.

I considered a Goryo's Vengeance direction, but Thud needs red and that deck has almost no red sources. The Grixis shell was the only direction where all three requested cards fit.

results.prompt: Brew me a Modern deck built around Fight Rigging, Turntimber Symbiosis and Slumbering Trudge.
results.text:
The deck is a brew: mono-green ramp built around Slumbering Trudge and Fight Rigging, with Turntimber Symbiosis as both a late-game spell and a land. Turn 1 Trudge for X=0 gives a 6/6 that never has to attack. Fight Rigging on turn 3 then adds a counter to make it 7/7 each combat, which lets me cast the hidden card free, often Craterhoof Behemoth, Ghalta or Primeval Titan. Mana dorks and Green Sun's Zenith carry the deck to those payoffs.

I considered three directions: a blue-green Neoform build borrowing that 230-list shell, a mono-green ramp deck, and a green-red aggro build. I chose mono-green because all three named cards are green, so it removes colour screw and the blue in Neoform adds nothing to these cards. Nothing in the tools shows these three cards together in any list, so this has no tested record. Its base is the Mono-Green Midrange shell (dorks, Boseiju, Green Sun's Zenith, Questing Beast, Old-Growth Troll). The deck runs 17.5 land-equivalents plus about 12 ramp creatures, a little under the 19.7 lands that shell averages, and that is the main thing to watch in play.

The deck passed `check_deck` with no warnings and was accepted. The win line of Trudge, Fight Rigging, the free hideaway cast and Craterhoof is complete by turn 5 in only about 9% of games. Tutors and card draw are not simulated, so that figure understates how often the line comes together.

results.prompt: Brew me a Legacy deck built around Apex Devastator, Call Forth the Tempest and Creative Technique.
results.text:
I built a red-green cascade brew on a Mono-Red Prison ramp base. It's accepted, but it's a brew, not a proven list, and the win line is unreliable: every card in the line is drawn by turn 6 in only about 4% of games.

I considered three directions:
1. **Red-green cascade ramp (chosen):** the only shell where all three cards fit and where Apex Devastator's four cascades are castable.
2. **Izzet tempo with Call Forth and Creative Technique:** cheap spells would feed Call Forth's damage, but Apex Devastator is green and drops out.
3. **Sneak and Show with Apex:** Show and Tell or Sneak Attack can put Apex in play for free, but that skips cast, so it loses the cascades that make Apex worth playing.

The deck runs 20 lands (12 Mountain, 8 Forest) and 11 mana sources (4 Chrome Mox, 4 Grim Monolith, 3 Lotus Petal) plus Llanowar Elves. The plan is to ramp to 10 mana by turn 5 or 6 and hardcast Apex Devastator, whose four cascades each cast a free spell under 10 mana. Creative Technique is the backup way to get Apex or Call Forth into play for free, and Call Forth finishes the board once cheap spells have been cast that turn. Sol Ring is banned in Legacy, so I didn't use it. The validator flagged Violent Outburst as an unusual choice, and I kept it as a cheap cascade enabler and answered that note.

Turn 1-2 mana; imprint a red or green card from hand to fix colors for GG/RRR costs.

results.prompt: Brew me a Legacy deck built around Arclight Phoenix, Buried Alive and Flow State.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and what real decks run alongside them.

Arclight Phoenix is a Pioneer/Modern Izzet Phoenix card, and Flow State is a Legacy tempo staple. Next I'll pull the Izzet Tempo and Dimir Tempo lists and the Legacy field to see which shell fits.

Three directions stand out. An Izzet base fits Phoenix and Flow State natively, but Buried Alive needs a black splash. A Dimir base fits Buried Alive natively, but Phoenix and Bolt need red. A Reanimator base fits Buried Alive but makes Phoenix a poor target. Next I'll check the spells that help the Phoenix turn: several cheap spells cast in one turn.

The type filter didn't return instants and sorceries, so I'll check the specific candidate cards by name instead.

Most cards check out as legal and in use. Expressive Iteration is banned, so I'll leave it out. Before choosing the splash, I want the odds of having both Buried Alive and a black source by turn 3 and turn 4.

Splashing black for Buried Alive is too unreliable: with four black sources, I'd have both Buried Alive and a black source by turn 4 only about 27% of the time. Dimir has native black and blue, so Buried Alive and Flow State are easy to cast, and Phoenix can be returned from the graveyard for free. I'll pull the Dimir Tempo list to borrow its shell.

Dimir has native black and blue and runs about 19.5 lands, so it's the right base. I'll build the deck: Buried Alive, Flow State, and four Phoenix. Phoenix stays in the library as a Buried Alive target. The red splash only covers Lightning Bolt and a hard-cast Phoenix. Before I check the deck, I'll look up the sideboard candidates I plan to use.

The deck passes check_deck with no errors or warnings. Next I'll confirm the Buried Alive timing, which is the main thing the deck depends on.

Buried Alive is castable by turn 3 about half the time, and Flow State helps dig for it. That is the real constraint on this plan, so I'll state it in the final answer. Submitting now.

The checker wants six or more enablers for the graveyard step. Buried Alive can't go above four copies, so I'll resubmit with a reason.

I built a Dimir brew around Arclight Phoenix, Buried Alive and Flow State. It is accepted with no warnings.

**Plan:** Buried Alive on turn 3 puts three Arclight Phoenix into the graveyard. On turn 4, casting three instants or sorceries (Brainstorm, Ponder and Lightning Bolt is the line) returns all three Phoenixes at beginning of combat with haste, for 9 flying damage. Flow State and the cheap cantrips find Buried Alive and fuel the three-spell turn, and Murktide Regent and Brazen Borrower give the deck some board presence.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three. An Izzet base fits Phoenix and Flow State, but splashing black for Buried Alive gave only about 27% odds of having both Buried Alive and a black source by turn 4. A Reanimator base makes Buried Alive work, but Phoenix is a poor target there. I chose the Dimir Tempo shell, which casts Buried Alive and Flow State natively. Phoenix only needs to sit in the library to be fetched, and it can return from the graveyard without mana. Red is a light splash for Bolt and a hard-cast Phoenix.

**Honest odds:** Buried Alive by turn 3 on the play is about 49%, and all of the line's cards together by turn 5 is about 2%. This is a fragile, high-variance deck. Phoenix is not in any real Legacy list, so there is no proven list behind it; the Izzet Phoenix and Reanimator lists I checked are the closest evidence. The sideboard is built to answer Dimir, Izzet, Sneak and Show, Oops All Spells, Ocelot and Doomsday.

results.prompt: Brew me a Vintage deck built around Goblin Welder, Legion Extruder and Sewer-veillance Cam.
results.text:
I built a blue-red Vintage version of the Goblin Welder, Legion Extruder and Sewer-veillance Cam loop. The deck is submitted and accepted as a brew.

**The plan:** Turn 1, a land and Mox Ruby cast Goblin Welder. Turn 2, Sewer-veillance Cam and Goblin Engineer come down, and Engineer tutors Legion Extruder into the graveyard. Welder then swaps Cam and Extruder back and forth. Each Extruder entry deals 2 damage, and Cam's enter/leave trigger untaps Welder, so the loop runs without spending mana. The deck's Force of Will, Force of Negation and free mana protect the turn-2 kill.

**Direction:** I considered three. A Lurrus-recursion shell would recast these cards, but Lurrus is white-black and clashes with Welder's red and Cam's blue. A red goblin-burn shell has too few payoffs and no loop without Cam. I chose the blue-red loop because it is the only option where all three requested cards work together and the loop is an infinite-damage kill. I borrowed the Force of Will and free-mana package from the Vintage field.

**Caveats:**
- Vintage has no Sewer Combo results. The shell comes from Legacy Sewer Combo lists, which I adapted.
- Odds are modest. Welder, Cam, and an Engineer or Extruder all show up by turn 3 on the play only 12.9% of the time, so the deck relies on the cheap draw spells to dig.
- The checker recommends about 20 lands. I kept 12 because the deck is a turn-2 combo with 12 fast-mana sources, and the land count is a deliberate choice rather than an oversight.
- Cryogen Relic and Ichor Wellspring stayed in on purpose: each draws when Welder moves it, so they replace themselves during the loop.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Ardent Recruit, Search Party Captain and Springleaf Drum.
results.text:
I built a mono-white artifact aggro deck around the three cards, with a 17-land mana base and a 15-card sideboard.

**Direction chosen:** Mono-white artifacts. I considered W/B Glintblade (its Glint Hawk and Kor Skyfisher shell is strong, but it needs black for Cast Down and Vault of Whispers) and W/U Synthesizer (more blue than the requested cards need). Mono-white was the most consistent: Ardent Recruit and Search Party Captain both want white creatures, and Battle Screech's flashback needs three white creatures to tap. The core borrows from the 5-0 Mono-White Aggro list (Thraben Inspector, Kor Skyfisher, Prismatic Strands, Battle Screech, Thraben Charm, Journey to Nowhere). Glint Hawk comes from the Glintblade and Synthesizer lists.

**The plan:** Turn 1 Thraben Inspector, turn 2 Springleaf Drum (tapping a creature that doesn't need to attack), turn 3 Battle Screech with a flashback that taps the two new Birds plus Thraben Inspector for four flyers. results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Aurora Eidolon, Sandstorm Eidolon and Spirit Mascot.
results.text:
I built a Boros (red-white) aggro deck, using the Boros Aggro shell as the base. I considered three directions: a Boros aggro shell, a Madness-style red burn deck (which can't cast the white cards), and a white-based deck splashing red. Boros was the only one where all three named cards work together, since Spirit Mascot and both Eidolons need red and white.

The plan is to curve out with cheap white creatures and Spirit Mascot, then use Battle Screech and its flashback to make four flyers. Its flashback exiles a card from the graveyard, which grows Mascot. Thrilling Discovery, Pursue the Past and Mascot itself are multicolored, so casting them returns an Eidolon from the graveyard. The honest caveat is that Pauper has very few multicolored spells, so the Eidolons are mostly 4-mana 2/2s with a late-game recursion bonus rather than a real engine.

The deck is 60 cards: 22 creatures, 19 spells and 19 lands (9 Plains, 6 Mountain, 4 Boros Garrison). The submission was accepted with no errors. The only check warning was white sources (13 versus about 16 in real Boros lists), which I accepted because the deck is white-heavy with Battle Screech and several white two-drops.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Living Death.
results.text:
I'll start by checking Living Death's exact text and what real decks run it with.

Living Death is a {3}{B}{B} sorcery that mass-reanimates. Next I'll look at the BG Survival and Reanimator shells and the reanimation and self-mill cards in Premodern.

The BG Survival list runs one Living Death, and Reanimator doesn't run it at all. Before choosing a direction I need the Premodern cards that feed a graveyard and the reanimation spells.

Living Death doesn't pair with a single fixed shell, so I'll gather the candidate pieces. First I'll check the mill and reanimation spells and the big creatures worth putting in the graveyard.

Buried Alive, Exhume, Reanimate, Phyrexian Delver and Gargantua all look useful alongside Living Death. I'll confirm the key ones' exact text and check for a few top-end creatures I haven't seen yet.

I'll check the three interaction spells I plan to use, then run draw odds for the core line.

The core line hits Buried Alive, Living Death and Dark Ritual together by turn 4 only about 13% of the time, so I'll plan on a turn 4–6 deployment. Next I'll check the sideboard candidates' legality and text.

Tormod's Crypt is the most-played card in the format, so I'll keep it in the sideboard as graveyard hate. Now I'll run the deck through the checker against the Reanimator mana base.

The checker passes with no errors. The two warnings are the 16-land count and Akroma having no white sources; I'll keep both on purpose and explain them. Submitting now.

The submission was rejected because one of the needs entries used a card name that isn't in the main deck. I'll fix the name and resubmit.

I built a mono-black Living Death brew, submitted as `brew` with Moneyball Black as the donor shell. It uses Buried Alive to put big creatures into the graveyard, Dark Ritual to reach five mana on turn 4, and Living Death to clear both boards while returning Akroma, Visara and Phyrexian Gargantua. Akroma then attacks with haste. Discard (Cabal Therapy, Withered Wretch, Ravenous Rats) and Smother/Snuff Out/Diabolic Edict handle the early turns.

I chose this direction over a BG build with Hermit Druid and Survival of the Fittest (the only real Living Death lists are BG Survival, with Living Death as a single copy) and over a blue control build, where Living Death has no creatures to bring back. Mono-black is the most consistent of the three.

Things to know before you play it:
- **Slow:** Buried Alive, Dark Ritual and Living Death all by turn 4 happens only about 13% of the time. The checker's full-line estimate is 2.6% by turn 5, so expect the win to come later more often than not.
- **Symmetric:** Living Death returns the opponent's creature cards too. Withered Wretch can exile their graveyard creatures first.
- **Mana:** the checker flagged 16 lands against a recommended ~24. I kept 16 because Dark Ritual and Twisted Abomination's swampcycling help, and the Reanimator list it compared against runs about 14.
- **Akroma:** she has no white sources, so she only enters through reanimation (Living Death, Buried Alive, Reanimate, Animate Dead).
